Break-glass administrative access to production infrastructure; restricted to a named allow-list of source IPs and requires JIT elevation.

frrImplementation: Meridian maintains an automated asset inventory pipeline that queries the underlying IaaS platform's resource-tagging API every 4 hours to enumerate all compute, storage, and network resources within the MSW authorization boundary.
frrValidation: The inventory pipeline's output is reconciled weekly against the cloud provider's billing/usage export as an independent cross-check for untagged or orphaned resources.
frrAssessment: The independent assessor sampled the automated inventory against a manual resource enumeration during the FY26 annual assessment and found no discrepancies.

frrImplementation: Data flows between the MSW application tier, database tier, and the underlying IaaS platform are documented in the Certification Package Overview's information-flow repository, with each flow tagged with a security category of Moderate.
frrValidation: Flow documentation is regenerated automatically from network policy configuration (security groups / firewall rules) on every production deployment to prevent drift between documented and actual flows.
frrAssessment: Assessor confirmed via network configuration review that documented flows match observed traffic patterns during the FY26 annual assessment.

frrImplementation: The single third-party information resource in scope (the underlying IaaS platform) is identified in the Certification Package Overview along with its FedRAMP Certification status; the outbound-only email delivery dependency is documented as a non-certified third-party resource with a documented use-case justification.
frrValidation: Third-party resource list is reviewed quarterly by the compliance team against the current vendor inventory.
frrAssessment: Assessor verified the underlying IaaS platform's FedRAMP Certification status directly against the FedRAMP Marketplace during the FY26 annual assessment.

frrImplementation: Authenticated vulnerability scanning is performed continuously across 100% of the MSW authorization boundary using an agent-based scanning tool integrated with the asset inventory pipeline.
frrValidation: Scan coverage is validated weekly by reconciling scan results against the current asset inventory to identify any unscanned assets.
frrAssessment: Assessor reviewed 90 days of scan coverage reports during the FY26 annual assessment and confirmed continuous full-boundary coverage with no unscanned assets identified.

frrImplementation: Meridian publishes an Ongoing Certification Report to the trust center every 2 weeks, consistent with the 20x Class C maintenance cadence, summarizing certification data changes, accepted vulnerabilities, and reportable incidents for the period.
frrValidation: Report publication is tracked via an internal compliance calendar with automated reminders; a missed publication triggers an internal escalation.
frrAssessment: Assessor confirmed a consistent 2-week publication cadence by reviewing the trust center's report history for the trailing 6 months.

frrImplementation: Significant Change Notifications include, at minimum, a description of the change, its effective date, an assessment of impact to Key Security Indicators, and any affected third-party information resources, delivered via the trust center notification mechanism.
frrValidation: A sample Significant Change Notification is retained in the trust center's assessment-reports repository for reference.
frrAssessment: Assessor reviewed the most recent Significant Change Notification during the FY26 annual assessment and confirmed it contained all required elements.

ksiImplementation: All MSW user accounts authenticate via WebAuthn-based passwordless credentials (platform or roaming authenticators) as the primary method; accounts unable to use passwordless methods fall back to a strong password combined with phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2 security key).
ksiValidation: The identity provider's per-user authenticator-type report is reviewed monthly to confirm passwordless/phishing-resistant coverage remains above the internal 95% target.
ksiAssessment: Assessor queried the identity provider's authenticator report directly during the FY26 annual assessment and independently confirmed 97% passwordless/phishing-resistant coverage across active accounts.
ksiTests: Monthly automated query of identity provider API for per-user authenticator method
Attempted login using a disallowed authentication method (SMS OTP) to confirm rejection

ksiImplementation: Administrative access to production infrastructure requires just-in-time role activation through the cloud provider's privileged-access-management service, with a maximum session duration of 1 hour and mandatory justification entry.
ksiValidation: PAM activation logs are reviewed weekly for sessions exceeding typical duration or lacking justification text.
ksiAssessment: Assessor sampled 30 days of PAM activation logs during the FY26 annual assessment and confirmed all elevated sessions were time-bound and justified.
ksiTests: Automated weekly query of PAM activation log for session duration and justification-field completeness

ksiImplementation: All data in transit is encrypted using TLS 1.2 or higher; all data at rest, including database volumes and object storage, is encrypted using AES-256 with keys managed through the cloud provider's FIPS 140-3 validated key management service.
ksiValidation: Automated configuration scanning confirms encryption-at-rest is enabled on 100% of storage resources on every deployment pipeline run.
ksiAssessment: Assessor reviewed configuration scan results and independently spot-checked 3 storage resources during the FY26 annual assessment, confirming encryption was enabled and using validated cryptographic modules.
ksiTests: Per-deployment automated configuration scan for encryption-at-rest status on all storage resources

ksiEvidence.evidenceDescription: Storage encryption configuration scan output, July 2026

ksiImplementation: All application, infrastructure, and identity-provider logs are forwarded in near-real-time to a centralized, tamper-resistant SIEM with a 13-month retention period.
ksiValidation: Log-forwarding agent health is monitored continuously, with automated alerting on any host that stops forwarding logs for more than 15 minutes.
ksiAssessment: Assessor confirmed SIEM ingestion coverage across a sample of infrastructure components and reviewed retention configuration during the FY26 annual assessment.
ksiTests: Continuous automated monitoring of log-forwarding agent health across all hosts

ksiImplementation: Network traffic between application tiers is restricted using security groups that default-deny all traffic except explicitly allow-listed ports and protocols documented in the Certification Package Overview.
ksiValidation: Security group configurations are scanned nightly against the documented allow-list; any drift generates an automated alert to the security operations team.
ksiAssessment: Assessor reviewed security group configurations and the nightly drift-detection alert history during the FY26 annual assessment and found no unresolved drift incidents.
ksiTests: Nightly automated diff of live security group rules against documented allow-list

ksiEvidence.evidenceDescription: Security group configuration export and drift-detection log, July 2026

ksiImplementation: Meridian follows a documented incident handling process that includes detection, containment, eradication, and reporting to affected federal customers and FedRAMP within required timeframes.
ksiValidation: The incident response process was exercised via a tabletop simulation in Q2 2026; findings were incorporated into an updated runbook.
ksiAssessment: Assessor reviewed the Q2 2026 tabletop simulation report and confirmed the incident reporting timeline met FedRAMP requirements.
